Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-02-14
Start: 11:00 AM PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Daniel (Redwood Content), Asha (Constellation Head of Product), Luis (Constellation CTO), Maya (Growth), Evan (Eng)

-- Auto Summary (generated) --
Constellation Health recounts moving their triage and summarization pipelines to Redwood Dedicated. They describe a 3-month pilot, concerns about PHI/data residency, and the decision to use Dedicated capacity with KMS integration. Outcome: throughput up 3x for peak hours, token cost down ~38% after batching and quantization guidance, approved marketing quotes and a desire for a podcast-style case study.

Topics covered:
- Why they chose Redwood over expanding internal GPU cluster
- Security requirements (SOC 2, SSO, KMS, audit trails)
- Performance metrics and real user impact
- How the marketing team wants to present the story

-- Transcript --
00:00 Sophie: Hi everyone, thanks for joining on Valentine's day, appreciate you all making time. we're going to record this session just for a short podcast style piece and also capture a couple of soundbites for the case study. if anyone needs to opt out, say so now.
00:07 Asha: No, we're good to record. Awesome. Thanks for having us.
00:09 Marcus: quick mic check, can you all hear me?
00:11 Luis: yep, loud and clear.
00:14 Sophie: great. so maybe we'll start with a bit of background — Asha, could you give 60 seconds on Constellation's product and what triggered the search for a better inference approach?
00:24 Asha: sure, yeah. so Constellation is a care coordination platform, we ingest tons of provider notes, referral docs, um, and the thing that pushed us to look was increasing latency at peak times — our on-prem gpus were fine most of the day but during morning huddles and chart review windows things would back up and stakeholders started to notice. also, the ops overhead was growing, right? keeping drivers, patching, you know the whole stack.
00:47 Sophie: awesome, and when you evaluated options were you leaning towards cloud-hosted endpoints or something more controlled?
00:52 Asha: initially we wanted to double down on our on-prem infra, but after a couple of prod incidents and the cost analysis it became clear pushing more infra wasn't the cheapest path. security is a big concern for us — PHI, SOC2, and data residency — so Redwood's Dedicated offering and VPC + KMS integration were big ticks.
01:12 Marcus: Luis, from an engineering lens, what were the must-haves?
01:16 Luis: low p95 latency under 450ms for the triage path, end-to-end encrypted at rest and in transit, and clear audit logs for every inference. we also needed to keep a degree of model determinism for downstream QA. the Redwood team was able to show us the dedicated topology and the KV cache behavior which made a lot of sense.
01:33 Evan: i remember the KV cache looked like it cut our repeated context costs by something like 20% right away, because we have a lot of repeated patient metadata across notes.
01:42 Marcus: yep that lines up. the caching plus prefix batching helps a lot when you have repeated headers.
01:47 Maya: from marketing I just want the story bits — when did you know it was working? any clear wins we can share?
01:52 Asha: yeah, the first real win was during a pilot week — we ran our overnight ingestion on Dedicated, and our throughput went from 900 documents/hour to around 2.7k, so about 3x. that cut our backlog and reduced the time care coordinators waited for summarized notes.
02:12 Luis: and on cost we were surprised — after Marcus and the Redwood team suggested quantization profile and batching tweaks we saw a rough 38% reduction in token-equivalent cost. part of that was switching to a quantized variant that preserved our extraction quality.
02:26 Marcus: to be clear, the quality checks were the most important step for us, we ran evals on the prompt set and tuned generation temperature and priors so the summaries stayed consistent.
02:36 Asha: there was pushback from the clinical team initially, they were worried about hallucinations. but the Redwood optimize tooling and the canary rollout backstops made it possible to ship with confidence — we rolled it to 10% traffic, watched eval scores and then ramped.
02:52 Sophie: nice, that's exactly the kind of narrative people want. any funny anecdotes from the pilot?
02:56 Luis: (laughs) yeah, one of our triage rules misinterpreted 'left' as a side-note about laterality and flagged a bunch of notes incorrectly, so we had to tighten the prompt instructions. we call it the left-right saga.
03:10 Asha: the care coordinators loved when summaries started including explicit 'action items' sections, that saved them a lot of reading time.
03:18 Daniel: good soundbite — "saved reading time" — we'll clip that.
03:22 Maya: on the marketing front, are there any constraints on what we can publish? legal/security approvals?
03:26 Luis: we need to redact PHI obviously, and legal wants to review quotes. otherwise we're fine. we also prefer that any published latency/cost numbers are presented as "based on internal workload — results may vary".
03:40 Sophie: understood. we'll send the draft and the audio to your legal and product for sign-off.
03:44 Asha: one quick technical Q — during the migration did you help with model compability? we had a few custom tokens in clinician notes, acronym expansions and such.
03:52 Marcus: yes we worked with your team to extend the tokenizer mappings and added a preprocessor step in the ingest pipeline to normalize the common acronyms. that was part of why the KS (sic KV) cache hit rates improved because we normalized prefixes.
04:06 Evan: the tokenizer fixes actually reduced OOV hits, so you could see improvements in extraction recall too.
04:12 Sophie: could you quantify any downstream user metrics — like reduced time per chart review or NPS changes?
04:18 Asha: we tracked two things — time-to-first-summary for new referrals dropped from an average of 18 minutes down to 6.5 minutes during peak windows; and internal satisfaction with the summaries (surveyed care coordinators) moved from 64% adequate to 87% adequate.
04:36 Daniel: those are great numbers for the case study. we'll make sure to format them as signed-off metrics.
04:40 Maya: for the podcast — what kind of format do you prefer? short episodes, more narrative or conversational?
04:46 Asha: conversational with a couple of highlight segments. maybe an opening "problem" section, then a 'how we evaluated' and finally 'results' plus a quick tip from engineering.
04:56 Sophie: perfect, we'll structure the episode that way. quick note, we'll ask you for two 10–15 second quotes we can overlay as intros/outros.
05:05 Luis: sure. i'll aim for a technical one and Asha will do a product one.
05:09 Sophie: okay, switching gears — security checklist. Luis, you said SOC 2 was required — did we go through SOC2 in the process?
05:16 Luis: yes, we got the SOC2 attestation docs from Redwood, and your KMS integration doc. we verified that the keys can be customer-managed and that the audit logs are delivered to our SIEM. that closed a lot of concerns.
05:27 Marcus: on the Dedicated side we also provided a VPC deployment diagram and the network ACL suggestions.
05:31 Evan: practically speaking, setup was about three weeks from signed SOW to traffic. most of that time was service account provisioning and network policy reviews.
05:40 Sophie: great. any blockers that other customers should watch for?
05:43 Luis: yes — inventory your lexicon and acronyms in advance, and validate PII/PHI redaction rules. those two things saved us time later.
05:54 Asha: and plan the rollout around your highest traffic windows so you reduce tail latency impact.
05:59 Daniel: excellent tips. we'll include a short sidebar in the write-up.
06:04 Sophia: (sic) small note on numbers — is the 3x throughput number cleared for public use?
06:10 Luis: yes, but we'd like the caveat 'on our workload and config' — we don't want readers to assume identical results.
06:18 Marcus: understood. we'll add the contextual line in the case study.
06:22 Maya: besides quotes, any assets you can provide? screenshots, before/after dashboards, or a short video clip?
06:27 Asha: we can share an anonymized dashboard screenshot and a quick clip of a care coordinator (consented) describing how it changed their day. we'll redact PHI first.
06:36 Sophie: lovely. now a quick run of potential marketing soundbites — Asha you mentioned "saved reading time" can you say that again in a sentence for the mic?
06:45 Asha: yeah, sure — "Redwood's solution saved our care coordinators hours each week by delivering concise, actionable summaries that eliminated a lot of manual reading".
06:58 Daniel: perfect, we'll tag that as quote Q1.
07:02 Luis: my short technical quote: "Moving to Redwood Dedicated let us meet our latency SLOs and reduce inference costs without sacrificing extraction fidelity".
07:15 Daniel: Q2 captured.
07:17 Evan: and my team can provide a short blurb about tokenizer work if you want a developer perspective.
07:22 Sophie: great, that's Q3. we'll get the audio files post-process and circulate.
07:27 Maya: one last product question — did you try Redwood Optimize recommendations, and were they automated or manual?
07:34 Marcus: we ran a one-off Optimize run and got suggested batching sizes and quantization profiles; implementation was manual with step-by-step guidance from our team and Constellation's engs. some customers have integrated the automated suggestions into their CI but your team preferred manual control for the pilot.
07:51 Asha: yes manual was better for us — clinical safety came first.
07:55 Sophie: amazing. ok let's do a quick recap then close — Daniel, can you outline the next steps for marketing?
08:02 Daniel: sure — 1) we'll edit the raw audio into a 18–22 minute podcast episode, 2) prepare an 800–1,000 word case study draft, 3) send both to Constellation's legal and product for sign-off, 4) finalize quotes and assets. timelines are in the next steps list.
08:22 Sophie: and from a technical follow-up Marcus will send the brief latency/cost bullet points and a small diagram of the dedicated topology.
08:30 Marcus: yep, sending that by end of week.
08:32 Maya: i'll coordinate internal approvals and send logo + brand guide.
08:36 Sophie: perfect. any final comments?
08:38 Luis: just thanks, it's been a smooth process overall. happy to help with the podcast.
08:42 Asha: yeah thanks everyone.
08:44 Sophie: great, we'll wrap. Daniel, mute and stop recording when you're ready.
